newsitem.title: GERMANY: Italy's Prodi - EMU progress better than expected.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi - EMU progress better than expected.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday the effectiveness of measures taken by Italy to gain entry into the single European currency were working better than expected.

"The results of the policies undertaken by Italy to step into the euro are even better than I thought," Prodi told a news briefing for Italian journalists after a meeting with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
Italy's Prodi - EMU progress better than =2
Prodi said Italy had already reached three of the core parameters required for EMU entry and that the fourth was "within reach".
Referring to Maastricht Treaty criteria on debt-to-gross domestic product ratio, he noted: "The stress in the treaty is on the trend, and for us the trend is downwards".
Prodi played down recent rumours that Italy may not be welcome in first batch of EMU entrants in 1999, referring directly to an article in the British Financial Times newspaper this week.
"These comments never make one happy but we are happy to see that the market believed my statements (subsequently on the matter) and not those in the FT," he said.
